choices.choice: Buenos Aires has longer daylight than London
choices.reason: At the December solstice, the Southern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun. Buenos Aires (35°S) receives more than 12 hours of daylight, while London (51°N) receives well under 12 hours (about 7-8 hours). So Buenos Aires has longer daylight than London.

At the December solstice, the hemispheres experience opposite extremes. London near 51°N has its shortest day (~7-8 hrs) while Buenos Aires near 35°S has a long summer day (~14 hrs). They are far from equal.
24-hour daylight only occurs at or beyond the polar circle (66.5°S for the December solstice). Buenos Aires at 35°S does not experience midnight sun.

choices.choice: London has longer daylight than Buenos Aires
choices.reason: At the December solstice, London is in its winter (shortest days ~7-8 hrs) while Buenos Aires is in its summer (longest days ~14 hrs), so London has shorter, not longer, daylight.
Tokyo is at ~35°N. December 21 is the Northern Hemisphere winter solstice, giving Tokyo its shortest day of the year (~9-10 hrs), not its longest.

Sydney is at ~34°S. December 21 is the Southern Hemisphere summer solstice, giving Sydney its longest day (~14-15 hrs). However, compared to June 21 in Tokyo, Sydney's longer day is comparable. But Sydney at 34°S gets ~14-15 hrs vs Tokyo at 35°N on June 21 also ~14-15 hrs. These are roughly equal, so neither is clearly 'longest' over the other without more precision.
June 21 is the Southern Hemisphere winter solstice. Sydney (~34°S) would have its shortest day (~10 hrs), not its longest.

June 21 is the Northern Hemisphere summer solstice. Tokyo (~35°N) has its longest day of the year (~14-15 hrs). Comparing the four options: Dec 21 Tokyo is winter (short day), June 21 Sydney is winter (short day), Dec 21 Sydney is summer (~14-15 hrs). June 21 Tokyo and Dec 21 Sydney are both summer solstices at similar latitudes (~14-15 hrs). These are essentially tied, but June 21 in Tokyo is a valid answer for longest daylight among the choices.

sourceDocuments.text: At the June solstice the Northern Hemisphere is tilted most toward the Sun, and the Southern Hemisphere away; the relation reverses in December. The June solstice gives the longest daylight of the year at ordinary northern midlatitudes and the shortest at southern midlatitudes. Seasons arise primarily from axial tilt, not Earth-Sun distance.
